title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR Resp.3 — God imputes to none unless he sinned in self or in another (Saul)
pass_a_gloss: GAR's third reply: God never imputes unless the person sinned in himself or in another tightly joined to him—as Saul's sin was laid on his sons, and as the law visits fathers' sins on children.
pass_b_english: GAR. Answer 3. God imputes sin to no one unless he has sinned either in himself, or in another, that is, unless either he has committed sin in himself, or another with whom he is closely joined; as he imputed Saul's sin to his sons, not because they themselves had committed it, but because their father had committed it. And likewise God testifies in the law that he visits the sins of the fathers upon the children.
source_text: GAR. Resp. 3. Deus nemini peccatum imputat, quin ille peccaverit vel in se, vel in alio, id est, quin vel in se peccatum commiserit, vel alius, quocum arcte coniunctus est; sicut Sauli peccatum filiis eius imputavit, non quia ipsi commisissent, sed quia pater eorum commiserat. Et item Deus testatur in lege, se visitare peccata patrum in filiis.

lemmas.latin: vel in se, vel in alio

choices.choice: No imputation without sin in self or closely joined other
